Kristies Lab · Circular event production

Every propdeserves asecondlife.

Our warehouse holds chairs, arches, backdrops, lights and objects that each lived through one event. Second Life gives every one of them a digital passport, so planners, suppliers and production teams can borrow them for free, reuse them, transform them, and add to their story.

How it works

From storage to stage, and back

Lending is free. You arrange and cover your own transport. In return, you help us write the next chapter of the prop's story.

  1. 01

    Scan or browse

    Every prop carries a QR code that opens its passport: materials, dimensions, condition, availability and what you may do with it.

  2. 02

    Request it

    Approved partners request a prop for an event, say whether they will reuse, adapt, dismantle or transform it, and accept the lending terms.

  3. 03

    Give it a new life

    Once approved, pick it up from the warehouse. Use it as it is, or rework it within the permissions on its passport.

  4. 04

    Add to its story

    Scan the code again after your event. Upload photos, say where it went and how it changed, then return it or record its final form.

Four ways to keep an object in circulation

Reuse

Take it as it is, for another event, another brand, another room.

Repair

Fix what was broken so the object can travel again.

Refurbish

Repaint, re-cover or re-light it to fit a new concept.

Repurpose

Dismantle or transform it into something new, and keep tracing its parts.

Second Life · version 2026-10

Lending terms

Second Life lends props from the Kristies Lab warehouse to approved B2B partners so they can be reused instead of discarded. This first year is a pilot, and these terms will evolve with what we learn together.

  1. 01

    Responsible use

    I will use this prop responsibly and only for the purpose stated in this request.

  2. 02

    Photo update

    I will upload photos and update the passport after use.

  3. 03

    Return or final status

    I will return the prop, or report clearly whether it was transformed, dismantled or kept for an approved reuse.

  4. 04

    Brand protection

    I will not reuse visible branding or confidential elements unless Kristies Lab approves it.

  5. 05

    Damage disclosure

    I will report any damage, missing parts or transformation.

  6. 06

    Free lending, own transport

    Second Life lending is free of charge. I arrange and cover pick-up, transport and return.

Who can borrow. Event planners, production companies, suppliers and collaborators approved by Kristies Lab, competitors included.

What each passport allows. Every passport lists what may be done with that prop: reuse as is, adapt, dismantle, transform, donate or recycle. Please stay within it, and ask the team if you want to go further.

Confidentiality. Some props come from private or confidential events. Do not share client names, original concepts or branded elements unless the passport shows them publicly.

Your data. We record who borrowed each prop, when and for what, so we can trace its journey. Photos you mark as shareable may appear on public passports and in Second Life communications.
